title: Food Preservation — Principles, Methods, Thermal and Non-Thermal Technology
shortDescription: Why food spoils, the principles of preservation and a map of thermal and non-thermal methods.
genZNote: Preservation is just convincing microbes, enzymes and oxygen to wait outside. D, z, F values are how you measure the bouncer.

sections.heading: Principles of Preservation
bullets: Prevention or delay of microbial decomposition (keep out, remove, hinder growth, kill).
Prevention or delay of self-decomposition (enzyme inactivation, antioxidants).
Prevention of damage by insects, animals and mechanical forces.
Hurdle approach: combine several mild barriers (temperature, aw, pH, preservatives, packaging).

sections.heading: Methods at a Glance
sections.body: Thermal metrics: D-value (time at a temperature to reduce microbes tenfold), z-value (temperature change to alter D tenfold), F-value (lethality equivalent, F0 at 121.1 °C with z = 10 °C). The 12D "botulinum cook" is the minimum for low-acid canned foods; pH 4.6 separates low-acid (pressure retort) from acid foods.

table.caption: Preservation map
rows: Blanching, pasteurization, sterilisation, canning, UHT, aseptic
Pasteurization 63 °C/30 min or 72 °C/15 s; commercial sterility 121 °C
Chilling (0–5 °C), freezing (−18 °C or below), cold chain
Freezing stops growth; does not kill all microbes
Salting, sugar (jam, preserves), pickling in brine
Class I: salt, sugar, spices, vinegar; Class II: benzoic, sorbic, SO2/sulphites, nitrite, propionates, nisin
Up to 10 kGy overall average dose per Codex
HPP, PEF, UV, cold plasma, ultrasound, membrane filtration

sections.heading: Thermal vs Non-Thermal
bullets: Thermal: reliable and cheap, may degrade vitamins, flavour and texture.
Non-thermal (high pressure, pulsed electric fields, UV, cold plasma, irradiation, ultrasonics, membrane filtration): retain freshness but need capital, validation and regulatory approval.
Selecting a method depends on food type, target microbe/enzyme, desired shelf life, cost and regulations. See Unit 10 for technology detail.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: Food preservation applies physical, chemical and biological methods to delay microbial, enzymatic and chemical spoilage and ensure safety and shelf life.
keyFacts: Class I vs Class II preservatives.

highYieldFacts: pH 4.6 divides acid and low-acid foods.
commonTraps: Do not say freezing sterilises food.
